plans.angle: RISK-FIRST. Users never run a Rust component until it has been proven equivalent to the Python one, and every switch can be reversed in seconds without logging out. Five rules make this work. (1) Freeze the Python 0.5 behavior as an executable oracle and as committed golden files before writing any Rust. (2) Port the pure core first and prove it with a differential harness: Python and Rust run on the same generated query, config and edit corpus, and every difference must either be zero or appear on a reviewed allowlist that names a parity-spec ID. (3) Switch one D-Bus component at a time (search provider first, then prompt box with settings) behind the unchanged bus names, object paths, .ini, desktop id and ~/.local/bin/llm-search path. Only the rendered .service Exec line changes, so rollback means re-rendering that line and killing the process. (4) While Python is still a rollback target, nothing Rust writes may stop Python from reading the config. Writes stay inside TOML 1.0 and the current schema, with no new agents.toml keys until Python is gone. (5) Bug fixes and behavior changes never ship in the same release as a cutover. Each is a separate, documented, allowlisted change after the component has soaked at parity.
plans.architecture:
CARGO WORKSPACE in the existing repo (one folder per crate, Cargo.lock committed, edition 2024, rust-version = "1.92", resolver 3):
- crates/core (agent-search-core, lib). Pure Rust with NO system libraries, so `cargo test -p agent-search-core` runs on any machine, including CI, with no GTK and no display. Modules:
  - query (Q-01/02, E-01)
  - effort (E-02/03)
  - ranker (R-01..06)
  - ids: blake2s-48 query key from the parameter block, not a truncated digest (ID-01/02)
  - catalog: models_from_info and Candidate, with gateway I/O behind a trait (G-01/02)
  - resolve (A-01)
  - urlfill: a hand-written port of str.format subset, quote(safe=''), urlsplit, parse_qsl, urlencode and urlunsplit. Not the url crate (U-01/02)
  - command: fill_command and command_for (C-01/02)
  - which: an injectable seam, used by tests the way launch.which is monkeypatched today (C-03)
  - config::{load, secrets, signature, migrate, defaults} (CF-01/02, S-01/02, SIG-01, M-01, RD-01)
  - edit::{scalar, structure, validate} on toml_edit (T-*, the new editor)
  - pyregex: a Python-re to fancy-regex translator plus validator
  - pycompat::{split, strip, splitlines, capitalize, lower}, with code-point tables generated from Python 3.14/Unicode 16 by a checked-in script.
  Activation in core returns an Action enum {Copy(text), Spawn{argv,cwd}, OpenUri(url), Nothing}. Executors are separate, so core stays pure and the oracle can compare actions without running them.
- crates/provider (bin `agent-search-provider`). Depends on gio/glib only, NOT gtk, to keep cold start and memory low.
  - A gio::Application subclass with app id io.github.oscillatingjem.AgentSearch.SearchProvider, flags IS_SERVICE and inactivity_timeout 60000, the same as Python (DB-01). Its .service Exec passes no --gapplication-service, also the same as today.
  - In ApplicationImpl::dbus_register it chains up, then calls connection.register_object("/io/github/oscillatingjem/AgentSearch/SearchProvider", iface). iface comes from DBusNodeInfo::for_xml using provider.py's INTERFACE_XML verbatim. The handler is a raw method_call, so error names and reply variants are under exact control (Failed or UnknownMethod, DB-12).
  - Each call takes `let _g = app.hold()` and keeps it until the invocation is answered (DB-04).
  - Every handler body is wrapped in catch_unwind and maps to org.freedesktop.DBus.Error.Failed. Core and executors run with clippy unwrap_used/expect_used denied.
  - LaunchSearch is a fire-and-forget DBusConnection::call to org.freedesktop.Application.ActivateAction('search',[<s>],{}) (DB-11).
  - URIs open through gio::AppInfo::launch_default_for_uri(url, None), as today.
  - Spawn uses std::process::Command with stdin, stdout and stderr on Stdio::null() and unsafe pre_exec(libc::setsid), because CommandExt::setsid is nightly-only. Each child is reaped with glib::child_watch_add, fixing L-02 zombies in long-lived processes.
  - Clipboard keeps the `wl-copy --` / `xclip -selection clipboard` subprocess contract (L-03).
  - Logging is a tiny stderr logger that prints 'llm-search: <msg>' at INFO, so journal greps keep working (DB-13).
- crates/app (bin `agent-search`). The libadwaita app with id io.github.oscillatingjem.AgentSearch and DEFAULT flags. local_command_line is never overridden, so --gapplication-service keeps working (PB-01).
  - Actions 'search'(s) and 'preferences'. A startup hold that is never released, matching today's lifecycle (PB-03/04).
  - Modules prompt (PB-*), settings (SW-* at parity, then the new editor), shortcut (gio::Settings with the relocatable custom-keybinding schema; the schema source is checked before Settings::new, and sync() runs before quit, SC-*), and css (identical strings, CssProvider::load_from_string).
  - Local options through add_main_option and handle_local_options: --check-config [DIR] (the whole-config validator, exit 0/1, replaces `llm-search test` on installs and the python3 tomllib comment hint), --set-shortcut BINDING and --remove-shortcut. These replace the installer's python3 ast.literal_eval helper (CLI-18).
- crates/parity (bin `agent-search-parity`, publish = false, never installed). Reads JSONL ops on stdin and writes JSONL results using exactly the protocol of tests/parity/oracle.py.
- tests/parity/: oracle.py (run with python3 -I against src/llm_search, with which, clock, HTTP, spawn, clipboard and open monkeypatched), gen_corpus.py (seeded generator), golden/*.jsonl (frozen expectations), deviations.toml (allowlist keyed by spec ID), run.sh (live differential run).
- bin/llm-search stays bash as deployment glue. It works before anything is compiled, and porting it adds risk with no user benefit. Its Python dependencies are removed. See install_and_distribution and the open questions.

CRATES (versions verified 2026-10-18):
- gtk = { package = "gtk4", version = "0.11.5", features = ["v4_14"] }, app crate only. v4_12 is the hard floor (CssProvider::load_from_string; FileDialog and UriLauncher need v4_10). v4_14 matches Ubuntu 24.04.
- adw = { package = "libadwaita", version = "0.9.2", features = ["v1_5"] }. AlertDialog needs v1_5. SpinRow, ToolbarView and NavigationView are v1_4. EntryRow and PasswordEntryRow are v1_2.
- glib, gio = "0.22.10".
- HTTP: soup3 = "0.9.0" (MSRV 1.92, async on the GLib main loop). TLS comes from glib-networking, so https gateways keep working as they do with urllib, the GNOME proxy settings apply, and only one small binding crate is added. Fallback: ureq 3.4.2 with rustls. The no-TLS ureq profile is rejected, because it would silently break https gateway URLs that work today.
- toml = "1.1.8" + serde (derive) for typed loading. toml_edit = "0.25.17" for all writes.
- fancy-regex = "0.19.2", wrapped by pyregex.
- percent-encoding = "2.3.2" with NON_ALPHANUMERIC minus -._~. The facts verify this equals quote(safe=''); glib::Uri::escape_string is equivalent but would pull GLib into core.
- serde_json = "1" for gateway JSON and the parity protocol.
- blake2 (RustCrypto, Blake2sVar with output size 6). The version is pinned when added and proven against the six golden vectors in ID-01.
- libc for setsid.
- Dev only: gtk4-macros #[gtk::test], gio::TestDBus. No proptest: the corpus is generated on the Python side, so Rust takes no extra dependencies.
- Avoided: zbus 6.0.0 (two days old, breaking changes, second connection) and search-provider 0.13.0 (zbus 5, second bus name, unwrap on the connection). Neither integrates with GApplication's hold/inactivity handling.

D-BUS APPROACH: gio for everything, one connection per process (GApplication's own), objects registered in dbus_register so they exist before the name is owned. GetInitialResultSet and GetSubsearchResultSet reply asynchronously after the gateway future resolves (0.5 s timeout as today). Calls are still processed in arrival order. The stored rows and prompt are replaced only when a reply is sent, so GetResultMetas semantics are unchanged (DB-08).

REGEX ENGINE: fancy-regex built with case_insensitive(true) and backtrack_limit, compiled ONCE at load. A translator turns Python-re semantics into fancy-regex syntax:
- `\Z` becomes `\z`. An unescaped `$` outside a class becomes `(?=\n?\z)`. `{,n}` becomes `{0,n}`. `\<` and `\>` become literals. A `[` inside a class is escaped.
- `\s` becomes `[\s\x1c-\x1f]`. `\w`, `\W` and `\b` are rewritten from a Python-isalnum class with lookaround, so combining marks and No/Nl digits behave like Python.
- `\N{NAME}`, octal escapes, (?a) and (?L) are rejected with a clear message.
Known residual difference: İ and ı case folding. A pattern that fails to compile or translate is reported with its rule index. During the parity phases it fails the search exactly as Python does when reached. Afterwards it becomes skip-and-report (a separate, allowlisted change). Fallback if the owner prefers PCRE semantics: glib::Regex.

CONFIG LOADING: serde structs mirror the dataclasses. They use #[serde(deny_unknown_fields)] on App and Rule only (as today), ignore unknown top-level and other-table keys, accept int or float for priority, weight and idle_minutes, and accept float or int for min_chars and max_rows (parity with Python's lack of type checks). Truthiness for enabled: a string 'false' counts as true. That case is captured as a golden and later becomes a validation warning. Aliases are lowercased, and the last lowercase collision wins. secrets.env and the migration are byte-exact ports.

EDITING: two layers, both on toml_edit::DocumentMut.
(a) scalar::apply(text, edits) reproduces today's observable contract for the P-01 keys: same value replacement with decor kept, missing key placed DIRECTLY below the header or id line (by rebuilding the table's key order; toml_edit appends at the end by default), missing table appended with '[t]  # added by the settings window', and a readback check with Python-style 1 == 1.0 leniency.
(b) structure:: implements add, delete and rename agent, arrays (multi-line layout kept via push_formatted with copied decor), command argv with nested optional groups, aliases, routing patterns and rules (addressed by index), and gateway including key_env.
validate:: runs the same loader the provider uses, plus regex compile, placeholder checks, alias targets, unique ids with no '|', and a TOML-1.0 emission check, all before any write. Writes go through a temp file in the same directory, opened with the existing mode, then fsync and rename. The rename goes to the symlink's target (fixes UP-01) as a scheduled, allowlisted change.

phases.name: Phase 0: Baseline, oracle and README fixes (Python 0.5.1)
phases.goal: Freeze current behavior as executable truth before any Rust exists, fix the known README errors for today's Python users, and verify the assumptions the rollback mechanism depends on.
deliverables: Owner-run toolchain install (needs sudo, so the owner does it): `sudo dnf install rust cargo gcc pkgconf-pkg-config gtk4-devel libadwaita-devel glib2-devel libsoup3-devel dbus-daemon xorg-x11-server-Xvfb`.
Tag the current main as v0.5.0 if it is not already tagged (local tag; push only after the owner says yes).

Extend the Python unittest suite to cover the spec's gaps, which pins behavior before porting: Gateway HTTP and cache timing with a fake clock and a local http.server; read_env_file parsing; the activate(), copy_prompt and command paths with spawn and clipboard captured; fill() normalization vectors from U-01; resolve() ordering (an alias falling through, step 3 before step 4); max_rows of 0 and 1; toml_edit insertion position, format_value output and line-ending normalization. Target: 35 tests grow to about 80, all green.

tests/parity/oracle.py: a JSONL op server over src/llm_search, run with python3 -I. Ops: parse, rank (ids, titles, subtitles, meta descriptions), resolve, fill_url, fill_command, command_for, activate (captured Action), load (normalized dump or error class plus message), read_env, set_secret (bytes plus mode), toml_apply (text or EditError), migrate, restore_defaults, re_search(pattern, text).

tests/parity/gen_corpus.py: a seeded generator for query terms (valid and invalid @ and ! tokens, Unicode words, Turkish I, ligatures, combining marks, \x1c-\x1f, \xa0, U+2028), config mutations of examples/config/agents.toml, model_info fixtures, edit lists, and regex probe strings. tests/parity/golden/*.jsonl: about 20k frozen cases plus every verified vector from specCore and specUi.

docs/PARITY.md: every spec behavior ID classified A (match exactly), B (deliberate difference introduced during the port, allowlisted) or C (bug kept at cutover and fixed afterwards), plus a mapping table from Python tests to Rust tests. deviations.toml starts empty.

Rollback-mechanism spike on Fedora 44 (dbus-broker): rewrite a rendered .service file's Exec in place, call org.freedesktop.DBus.ReloadConfig, kill the process, and confirm the next activation uses the new Exec with no logout. Also confirm that GNOME Shell needs no restart when only Exec changes.
Baseline measurements script (scripts/bench.sh): provider cold-start-to-first-reply, prompt box cold start and PSS, and per-keystroke rank latency. The numbers become the Rust exit targets.

README and docs fixes (0.5.1, Python-era). Requirements become GNOME 46+, libadwaita 1.5+ and GTK 4.12+. Fedora 40+ replaces 39+. Debian 13+ / Ubuntu 24.04+ replaces Debian 12+, because Debian 12 has libadwaita 1.2. The Debian/Ubuntu install line becomes `sudo apt install python3-gi gir1.2-glib-2.0 gir1.2-gtk-4.0 gir1.2-adw-1 wl-clipboard`, and check_requirements also checks the Gtk 4 and Adw typelibs. Stale docs fixed: USAGE.md (the category icon opens the prompt box), TROUBLESHOOTING.md (config reloads on change; current id format), CONFIGURATION.md ('three files' becomes two).
docs/DESIGN.md: a Mermaid diagram of the target architecture and the per-component cutover state machine.
phases.user_visible_state: Python 0.5.1, identical behavior. Only the README requirement table, a stricter requirement check (it now warns about the missing Gtk 4 and Adw typelibs) and the corrected docs change.
phases.parity_and_tests: There is no Rust yet. The oracle is checked against the existing 35 tests and the new tests: oracle output for each test's inputs must equal what the test asserts. Goldens are generated twice from different processes and must be byte-identical, which proves the oracle is deterministic.
exit_criteria: All Python tests pass (35 existing plus the new ones).
The golden corpus is committed, regenerates deterministically, and covers every spec ID in class A, with a coverage report listing IDs.
The ReloadConfig plus Exec-swap spike is confirmed on Fedora 44 with no logout, or a documented alternative (for example, renaming the rendered file and re-linking) is proven.
Baseline numbers are recorded in docs/PARITY.md.
phases.rollback: Only docs and tests changed. Revert the commit or reinstall v0.5.0.

phases.name: Phase 1: Rust core at parity (no user change)
phases.goal: Implement agent-search-core and prove it equals Python on queries, ranking, ids, aliases, the gateway catalog, URL and command templating, activation decisions, config and secrets loading, signature and migration.
deliverables: Workspace skeleton: Cargo.toml, crates/core, crates/parity, rust-toolchain (none; MSRV is declared), Cargo.lock.

CI (GitHub Actions, runs-on pinned to ubuntu-24.04): fmt, clippy -D warnings, core tests on the 1.92 MSRV and on stable, goldens replay, and the existing Python tests. A Fedora container job builds the whole workspace.

Core modules as listed in the architecture. pycompat tables (isspace, Python title-casing for capitalize, and splitlines breakers) are generated by scripts/gen_unicode_tables.py from Python 3.14 and checked in.
pyregex translator and validator, with fancy-regex 0.19.2.

Every one of the 35 original tests is ported 1:1 into crates/core/tests/{parse,rank,command,settings_load,url}.rs with the same names and the same fixtures (examples/config/agents.toml and the model_info data from test_search.py setUp). The settings tests that need the writer are ported in Phase 2. The Phase 0 additions are ported too.
agent-search-parity binary plus tests/parity/run.sh, which runs the oracle and Rust on a fresh seed and diffs the results.
phases.user_visible_state: Unchanged Python 0.5.1. The Rust code exists only in the repository.
phases.parity_and_tests: Three layers. (1) Golden replay in CI: Rust must reproduce every committed golden exactly (about 20k cases). (2) A live differential run of run.sh with new seeds: 200k query x config cases locally per change set and 1M before exit, with zero unexplained diffs. (3) Exhaustive per-code-point checks against Python for split, strip, capitalize and lower, plus single-char \w, \s, \d and \b probes through pyregex for all 0x110000 code points. Regex parity uses the shipped example patterns plus a curated set of about 300 Python-re constructs over Unicode probe strings. The İ/ı case-folding difference is the only expected allowlisted regex difference. Any class B entry needs a deviations.toml line naming the spec ID and a rationale.
exit_criteria: All ported tests pass on 1.92 and stable.
Golden replay passes 100%.
1M live differential cases with 0 non-allowlisted diffs, and deviations.toml reviewed by the owner.
Exhaustive Unicode table checks pass.
Core has no unwrap or expect outside tests (clippy enforced).
phases.rollback: Nothing is installed. Abandoning the work leaves Python untouched.

phases.name: Phase 2: Rust config writer at parity, Python-readable
phases.goal: Port toml_edit.apply, update(), set_secret and restore_defaults onto the toml_edit crate, so that every write the current settings window can make produces the same file Python would produce (or an allowlisted difference), and every Rust output stays loadable by Python.
deliverables: edit::scalar with the exact placement and decor rules from T-04..T-10: value replaced with indent, separator and suffix comment kept; missing key directly under the header or id line; missing table appended with the marker comment; readback check with Python-style numeric leniency; same EditError message texts (they are shown in toasts).

config::update with atomic writes: temp file in the same directory, existing mode kept, fsync, rename. Symlink behavior stays the same as Python here (replace the link) in this phase, recorded as class C.
set_secret with the same line semantics. Mode 0600 is set at creation (O_CREAT 0600 before writing, so no 0644 window), recorded as class B.

edit::structure API (not yet wired to UI): add, delete and rename [[app]]; set arrays; set the command argv with nested groups; set aliases; edit rules by index; delete keys. Golden round-trip fixtures cover comments above, inside and after blocks.
edit::validate: the whole-config validator, shared with --check-config later.

Ported settings tests: edits_apply_and_keep_every_comment, only_the_edited_lines_change, missing_gateway_table_is_added, unknown_agent_is_refused_and_file_untouched, multiline_values_are_refused, restore_defaults_resets_general_but_keeps_agents_rules_and_gateway, legacy_settings_file_is_migrated_once, signature_changes_on_update, set_secret_keeps_other_lines_and_mode.
phases.parity_and_tests: Edit differential: for each corpus file (the example, about 50 mutated variants and pathological inputs such as CRLF files, quoted keys, multi-line arrays, fake headers inside strings and U+2028) and each generated edit list of P-01 key types, compare the Python and Rust output text byte for byte, or the EditError class. Expected allowlisted differences: non-ASCII written as UTF-8 instead of \uXXXX (T-01); astral characters now succeed instead of failing; float formatting, where toml_edit writes 1e16 and Python writes 1e+16 (30.0 must stay '30.0'); CRLF preserved instead of normalized (T-10); fake-header spurious errors gone (T-02). Cross-readability gate: every Rust output, scalar and structural, must parse with Python tomllib and load with config.load, and the result must equal the Rust loader's view. This is what makes rollback safe while both engines coexist. Structural edits: comment-preservation property tests check that lines outside the edited entity are byte-identical.
exit_criteria: All 9 ported settings tests pass.
The edit differential has 0 non-allowlisted diffs over at least 50k edit cases.
100% of Rust outputs pass the Python tomllib plus config.load cross-check.
Structural goldens are reviewed by the owner on the real ~/.llm-search/config/agents.toml (on a copy).

phases.name: Phase 3: Rust search provider, shadow then cutover (0.6.0)
phases.goal: Ship agent-search-provider behind the unchanged bus name and object path, prove D-Bus-level parity, and make it the active provider with one-command rollback to Python.
deliverables: crates/provider as described in the architecture, with the gateway on soup3 (async, 0.5 s timeout, 60 s cache and 30 s back-off). The C-class behaviors are kept at cutover, including the 'first 60 s after boot' quirk, which is emulated by starting the clock at process start.

D-Bus parity test (tests/dbus_parity.sh plus a Rust integration test using gio::TestDBus). On a private bus it activates the Python provider, replays a scripted call sequence (GetInitialResultSet, GetSubsearchResultSet, GetResultMetas including unknown ids, ActivateResult with spawn, URL and clipboard redirected to recorder stubs through PATH and a fake handler, LaunchSearch observed by a fake prompt-box name, unknown method, an injected bad regex), and records GVariant text replies. It repeats this with the Rust provider and diffs the two. It also checks the 60 s idle exit and the restart of the hold-release timer.

Dev shadow name: a .Devel provider build installable next to the real one, plus `llm-search query --compare WORDS` that calls both and prints any difference. The owner runs it on real use for the soak period. Prompts stay local and are never logged.

Installer engine selection: `llm-search install --provider=rust|python` stores the choice in $LLM_SEARCH_HOME/state/install/engine.conf. Binaries are copied to $LLM_SEARCH_HOME/state/bin/<version>-<shortsha>/ and the last two versions are kept. The rendered SearchProvider.service gets Exec=/usr/bin/env LLM_SEARCH_HOME=@HOME@ <state/bin/...>/agent-search-provider. The installer then calls ReloadConfig, and pkill matches both generations ('-m llm_searc[h]' and 'agent-search-provide[r]').

Preflight gate before switching: `agent-search-parity --check-user-config` runs the user's own agents.toml (its patterns, aliases and agents) through oracle versus Rust on a probe corpus. The switch is refused, with the differences printed, unless --force is given.

`llm-search rollback` sets the provider (and later the prompt box) back to python, or to the previous Rust version if Python is not present. `llm-search status` prints which engine is active per component.
phases.user_visible_state: 0.6.0. By default Python is still active. The owner opts in with `llm-search install --provider=rust`, and from then on GNOME Shell search is served by Rust: faster cold start, same rows, same ids, same launches. The prompt box and settings window are still Python. No logout is needed in either direction.
phases.parity_and_tests: Core parity is inherited from Phases 1-2. Added here: the D-Bus replay diff must match exactly on reply types and values (the only allowed difference is result-id hash bytes if a golden mismatched, and none is expected because blake2s-48 is ported exactly). Integration tests run in CI under dbus-run-session. Manual checklist on Fedora 44 / GNOME 50: category appears, rows match the Python screenshots for 20 reference queries, activation of each agent type, LaunchSearch opens the Python prompt box with the full query, journal lines prefixed 'llm-search:'. Soak: at least 7 days of daily use with --compare showing 0 differences.
exit_criteria: The D-Bus replay diff is clean.
Cold start to first reply is at or below the Python baseline, and PSS is at or below the Python baseline (expect clearly lower).
The 7-day soak has 0 differences and no crash in the journal (a panic would show as a Failed reply plus a log line).
Rollback is rehearsed 3 times: rust to python to rust, each under 5 s and with no logout.
phases.rollback: `llm-search rollback` or `llm-search install --provider=python`. It re-renders the Python Exec line, reloads the bus config and kills the Rust process. The config files were never written by the provider apart from the legacy migration, which already happened on 0.5. Worst case: `git checkout v0.5.1 && ./install.sh`.
phases.estimate: 2-2.5 weeks of work plus a 1-2 week soak

phases.name: Phase 4: Rust prompt box plus settings window at parity (0.7.0)
phases.goal: Replace the resident Python prompt box process, which also hosts the settings window, with agent-search at feature parity. This includes the current three settings pages and the shortcut dialog, so the switch changes the engine without changing the UI.
deliverables: crates/app prompt module, an exact port of PB-01..18: window structure, placeholder and hint strings, CSS, capture-phase keys, focus-out dismiss, BROWSE selection, no-wrap move, idle timer through timeout_add_seconds_local. The idle timer is cancelled after presenting the settings window (avoids the PB-15/SW race, class B).

Settings parity port of SW-01..25: General, Agents and Gateway pages, the restore dialog (AlertDialog), the folder chooser (FileDialog; the '~2' prefix bug is fixed with a separator check, class B), the gateway Test button running async (no UI freeze), the toast texts, and the shortcut dialog with GTK accelerator_name and identical capture rules.
shortcut module on gio::Settings with an availability check, the same list order and the 'Agent Search' name.
Local options --check-config, --set-shortcut and --remove-shortcut.

Installer: `--prompt=rust|python`, rendering AgentSearch.service Exec=/usr/bin/env LLM_SEARCH_HOME=@HOME@ <state/bin/...>/agent-search --gapplication-service. pkill matches both generations, including a resident Python box (it can be resident for up to 30 minutes otherwise). The desktop file Exec (~/.local/bin/llm-search prompt) is unchanged.

UI tests: #[gtk::test] under xvfb-run with GSK_RENDERER=cairo, covering row building, key handling (Esc, Ctrl+comma, Tab, Up and Down), selection movement, entry clearing after send, the hide-on-close lifecycle, and settings-page construction from fixture configs. gio::TestDBus tests cover ActivateAction('search') and 'preferences' and `gapplication action` argument quoting.
phases.user_visible_state: 0.7.0. The owner opts in with `--prompt=rust`. The prompt box and settings look and behave the same, but open faster and use less memory. The search provider can be Rust or Python independently, and all four combinations are supported and tested.
phases.parity_and_tests: The window logic consumes core (already proven), so parity here is about UI contracts. (1) Unit and UI tests reproduce each PB and SW behavior ID. (2) The settings window's writes go through edit::scalar, which was proven in Phase 2, and an end-to-end test drives each settings widget and compares the resulting agents.toml with the Python settings window's output for the same action (both scripted, the Python side through the oracle's toml_apply with the same edit tuple). (3) A manual parity checklist runs side by side with screenshots: Python box and Rust box on 20 reference queries, every keyboard path, restore defaults, shortcut set and remove, folder picker, gateway test. (4) Soak: at least 7 days as the daily driver, with the provider also on Rust.
exit_criteria: Every PB and SW item on the checklist passes.
The UI test suite is green in CI (xvfb).
Prompt box cold start is at or below 150 ms on the owner's machine (the review estimate is about 90-110 ms) and resident PSS is at or below the Python baseline.
The 7-day soak has no crashes or stuck-resident processes.
Rollback is rehearsed for every combination of provider and prompt-box engine.
phases.rollback: `llm-search install --prompt=python` or `llm-search rollback`. The Phase 2 cross-readability gate guarantees that any agents.toml or secrets.env the Rust settings wrote is read by Python.

phases.name: Phase 5: Full settings editor, Rust-only feature (0.8.0)
phases.goal: Build the planned editor so that everything in agents.toml can be edited, with whole-config validation before every save, while staying inside the schema Python can still read so that rollback stays possible.
deliverables: Agents page as an AdwNavigationView (v1_4) with a drill-down page per agent.

Agent actions: add (from a template or by duplicating), delete (AlertDialog confirm, which shows aliases that would dangle), and rename the id (offers to rewrite aliases that target it; rejects '|', duplicate ids and empty ids).

All agent fields are editable: name, url (with live placeholder check), command argv editor (an ordered list of items, each a plain argument or an optional group of arguments, with reorder and a live preview of the argv for a sample prompt), cwd, requires (with installed or missing status), description, icon, tags, models, efforts, priority, copy_prompt and enabled. Two supported routes. Both run the same ./install.sh, and both keep today's per-user layout: nothing goes to /usr, and sudo is needed only for distro packages.

A) FROM SOURCE. The toolchain must be rustc/cargo 1.92 or newer, the MSRV of gtk4 0.11 and glib 0.22. Runtime libraries are always the distro's own (dynamic linking).

- openSUSE Tumbleweed: `sudo zypper in rust cargo gcc pkgconf-pkg-config gtk4-devel libadwaita-devel glib2-devel libsoup-devel wl-clipboard`. The libsoup-devel name is unverified.
Test-only extras: dbus-daemon and Xvfb (Fedora dbus-daemon and xorg-x11-server-Xvfb; Debian dbus-daemon and xvfb).

Regex dialect: Python re semantics are emulated through a translator over fancy-regex. A few constructs (\N{NAME}, octal escapes, (?a), (?L)) are rejected with a message, and İ/ı case folding differs. --check-config and the install preflight report any user pattern this affects.
risks_and_mitigations: Regex semantics drift breaking users' routing silently. Mitigations: the translator, exhaustive per-character class checks against Python, a corpus of about 300 constructs, and a preflight that runs the user's own patterns through Python and Rust and refuses the switch on any difference. Fallback: glib::Regex (PCRE2) if the owner values PCRE closeness over backtrack limits.

The rollback assumption fails, for example dbus-broker not picking up a rewritten .service until relogin. Mitigation: the Phase 0 spike proves it with ReloadConfig on Fedora 44 before any Rust ships, and an alternative of renaming and re-linking the rendered file is ready.

The Rust writer produces files the Python fallback can't read (TOML 1.1 constructs, new keys), so rollback itself would break. Mitigations: a cross-readability gate on every writer output in CI, a schema freeze until 1.0, TOML-1.0-only emission, and a one-time agents.toml backup before the first structural write.

Python-isms (str.split whitespace set, capitalize title-casing, full lowercase, code-point lengths, str.format, urllib normalization) are reimplemented subtly wrong. Mitigations: tables generated from Python, exhaustive code-point tests, and golden plus live differential runs with fresh seeds.

toml_edit decor pitfalls: Array::fmt collapsing, push not copying the multi-line layout, comments after a deleted [[app]] staying with the next header, and the append-at-end default for keys. Mitigations: explicit key reordering to keep below-header placement, push_formatted with copied decor, round-trip goldens on real configs, and an owner review of diffs on their own file.

A panic in a GTK callback or D-Bus handler aborts the process, where PyGObject merely printed the exception. Mitigations: catch_unwind at every handler boundary, unwrap and expect denied by clippy outside tests, every launch, save, regex and gateway error mapped to a toast or a Failed reply, and fuzzed config inputs into load and validate.

Distro toolchain gaps: Ubuntu 24.04 has no rustc 1.92 and Debian 13 has 1.85. Mitigation: prebuilt tarballs built on pinned ubuntu-24.04 with v4_14 and v1_5, documented rustup and backports paths, and an MSRV CI job. Raising features later drops distros (BIND_NOW load failure), so a feature bump needs an explicit README update.

ubuntu-latest moves to 26.04 in Oct-Nov 2026 and would silently raise the binary baseline to glibc 2.43 and libadwaita 1.9. Mitigation: pin runs-on: ubuntu-24.04, plus a release smoke test on Debian 13 and Ubuntu 24.04 containers.

gtk-rs churn: 0.11.x patch releases have added and reverted APIs, and 0.12/0.23 is coming. Mitigations: commit Cargo.lock, use --locked builds, plan one upgrade task per GNOME cycle, and avoid newly added APIs.

GtkShortcutLabel is deprecated since 4.18, while AdwShortcutLabel needs libadwaita 1.8, above the v1_5 baseline. Mitigation: keep GtkShortcutLabel behind a small wrapper and swap it when the baseline reaches v1_8.

Scope and fatigue for one maintainer: the estimates total about 16-21 working weeks before soaks. Mitigations: each phase ships value or proof on its own, Phases 3-4 can stop at 'Rust provider only' indefinitely, the Phase 5 editor can ship incrementally (agents first, then routing), and soak periods double as rest from the codebase.

Blocking or slow work on the main loop: the gateway, regex backtracking and child processes. Mitigations: async soup3 with a timeout, a fancy-regex backtrack_limit with the error mapped to 'no match plus warning', and a child watch for reaping.
Prompt privacy during shadow testing. Mitigation: --compare and the preflight run locally, never log prompts, and the corpus is synthetic.

plans.angle: USER-CONTINUITY-FIRST. Each phase ends with a working installed app. The D-Bus names, paths, desktop id, ~/.local/bin/llm-search path, gsettings shortcut and ~/.llm-search layout never change, so the owner's shortcut, GNOME search and agents.toml keep working through every swap. The lever is that GNOME, the shortcut and the desktop file reach both processes only through stable D-Bus names and one CLI path, so each implementation can be swapped by re-rendering a .service Exec line, one process at a time. The order is: (1) the prompt box and settings window go first, because that is the visible cold-start win and the base for the new editor; (2) the search provider and CLI/installer follow quickly, and Python is deleted; (3) the full settings editor is built only on the Rust codebase. Only Phase 1 has both implementations installed, and Python is feature-frozen at v0.5.0 from Phase 0, so "maintaining both" means keeping the frozen Python half loadable, not developing it. Phases 1 and 2 are strict parity, with the parity check defined below. Behavior fixes wait until Python is gone (Phase 4), except fixes for crashes and hangs. The config schema stays frozen until 1.0, so rolling back to the v0.5.0 tag stays possible at every phase.
plans.architecture:
WORKSPACE (repo root Cargo.toml; Rust and Python live side by side until the end of Phase 2; edition 2024, rust-version = "1.92", Cargo.lock committed, every build uses --locked):
- crates/core (lib `agent_search_core`, no GTK, no I/O side effects behind seams). Modules:
  - pystr: Python-compatible str.split/strip/splitlines whitespace sets; lower() and capitalize() titlecase special table, generated from Python 3.14 / Unicode 16 and checked in.
  - query: parse, EFFORTS and EFFORT_ALIASES.
  - ranker: suggest_effort, clamp_effort, matched_tags, rank, Row title/subtitle, resolve.
  - ids: result_id/parse_result_id, using blake2 Blake2sVar::new(6), not truncated BLAKE2s-256.
  - catalog: app_candidates, models_from_info.
  - gateway: cache state machine using Option<Instant>; fetch is behind a trait so tests inject responses.
  - launch: fill() as a hand-written urlsplit/parse_qsl/urlencode/urlunsplit pipeline. The WHATWG url crate is deliberately not used. Percent-encoding uses glib::Uri::escape_string semantics, verified identical to quote(safe=''), so core uses the percent-encoding crate with the same set to stay GTK-free. Also fill_command, command_for, and which() behind an injectable Which trait (the seam Python tests monkeypatch).
  - config: typed load via toml 1.1.8 + serde, with custom deserializers for int-or-float (priority, weight, idle_minutes, min_chars, max_rows held as f64 to match Python comparisons). Also LLM_SEARCH_HOME rules, read_env_file, set_secret (made atomic), signature, migrate_legacy_settings, restore_defaults.
  - pyre: Python-re compatibility layer over fancy-regex.
  - edit: ConfigDocument over toml_edit 0.25.17. Phase 1: scalar set with the Python placement contract. Phase 3: full structural ops.
  - validate: whole-config diagnostics with file spans from toml::Spanned / de::Error::span.
- crates/cli → binary `llm-search`. Links glib/gio/soup3 only, never GTK, so the installer can start and print missing-library hints on a machine without libadwaita. Rust links with BIND_NOW, so a GTK-linked binary would not even exec there. Subcommands: install, uninstall, status, query, prompt|open, check, test (alias of check), restart, help, plus the hidden `search-provider`, which the provider .service Exec runs.
- crates/ui → binary `agent-search`: the adw::Application prompt box, settings window and shortcut dialog. It is started by D-Bus with --gapplication-service. It does not override local_command_line and does not set IS_SERVICE in flags, so GLib parses the switch.

PROCESS AND D-BUS MAPPING (contracts unchanged):
- Search provider: gio::Application subclass with app id io.github.oscillatingjem.AgentSearch.SearchProvider, flags IS_SERVICE, inactivity_timeout 60000. It does not use adw::Application, so no GTK init and less memory. The object is registered in ApplicationImpl::dbus_register through DBusConnection::register_object(path from the app id, iface parsed from the same INTERFACE_XML), with typed_method_call(...).invoke_and_return_future_local, so the gateway fetch is awaited without blocking the loop. Each call holds an ApplicationHoldGuard for its duration, which reproduces the hold/release-per-call idle behavior. Errors map to org.freedesktop.DBus.Error.Failed or UnknownMethod. No unwrap is allowed in handlers, and catch_unwind sits at the handler boundary. zbus and the search-provider crate are rejected: they need a second connection and well-known name, zbus 6.0.0 shipped two days ago with breaking changes, search-provider is pinned to zbus 5, and neither integrates with GApplication's idle timeout.
- Prompt box: adw::Application with id io.github.oscillatingjem.AgentSearch and actions search(s) and preferences (plus a new internal 'quit', used by restart and install). It reproduces PB-01..PB-18 exactly: same widgets, CSS, key handling and idle timer.
- Settings window: adw::Window, ToolbarView, ViewStack. Phase 3 adds an adw::NavigationView (libadwaita 1.4) for the agent, alias and rule subpages, and adw::AlertDialog (1.5) for confirmations.
- CLI `prompt`: calls org.freedesktop.Application.ActivateAction('search', [<s>], platform-data) through gio. platform-data carries activation-token / desktop-startup-id taken from XDG_ACTIVATION_TOKEN / DESKTOP_STARTUP_ID, matching gapplication. With no TEXT it calls Activate. If the name cannot be activated, it falls back to exec'ing agent-search.
- Shortcut: gio::Settings, after a SettingsSchemaSource lookup so a missing schema does not abort. Then gio::Settings::sync() before quit. The bash remove_shortcut dependency on python3 ast.literal_eval goes away.

CRATES (latest stable as of 2026-10-18):
- gtk4 0.11.5, features ["v4_14"] (hard minimum v4_12; v4_14 matches Ubuntu 24.04)
- libadwaita 0.9.2, features ["v1_5"] (needed for AlertDialog; 0.9.0 is yanked)
- glib / gio 0.22.10
- soup3 0.9.0 for the gateway HTTP: GNOME-native, async on the GLib loop, TLS through system glib-networking, no tokio or rustls. The 0.5 s timeout is enforced with a gio::Cancellable plus a glib timeout, because Session timeouts are whole seconds. The timeout covers DNS too, which fixes that gap. Fallback: ureq 3.4.2 (default-features=false, json) on gio::spawn_blocking, which only works if the gateway is always plain-HTTP localhost.
- toml 1.1.8, toml_edit 0.25.17, serde 1 (derive), serde_json 1
- fancy-regex 0.19.2 (it pulls in regex 1.13.1)
- blake2 0.10.x (verify the latest patch at Phase 1 start)
- percent-encoding 2.3.2
- libc 0.2 (setsid in pre_exec; already a transitive dependency)
- Dev dependencies: none beyond std; gtk4-macros #[gtk::test] and gio::TestDBus come with the main crates.

REGEX: pyre::compile(pattern) translates Python-only syntax, then builds with fancy_regex::RegexBuilder::new(p).case_insensitive(true).backtrack_limit(100_000).
- Translations: \Z → \z; \< and \> → literal < and >; {,n} → {0,n}; a bare '[' inside a class is escaped; Python's unanchored '$' (no MULTILINE) → (?=\n?\z).
- Rejected with a precise message: \N{NAME}, the (?a) and (?L) flags, octal \0 escapes, mid-pattern global flags.
- Accepted with documented differences: Unicode \w/\b on combining marks and superscripts, \s on U+001C..U+001F, and İ/ı case folding.
- Every pattern is compiled once at config load. A pattern that fails to compile is disabled (never matches), logged once, and reported by `llm-search check` and the settings window. BacktrackLimitExceeded counts as no match and is logged.
- Phase 0 audits the owner's real patterns and the shipped examples against Python re over a prompt corpus. The audit is a golden test.

CONFIG LOADING: core::config::load(dir) returns (Config, Vec<Diagnostic>).
- Loads that succeed in Python produce the same values.
- Loads that are fatal in Python become lenient where the meaning is unambiguous. Unknown [[app]]/[[routing.rule]] keys → warning. A string where a list is expected → one-element list plus a warning. A non-bool `enabled` follows Python truthiness plus a warning. NaN priority → 0 plus a warning.
- Missing id, name, tag or patterns still makes that entry invalid. The entry is skipped with a diagnostic; the whole load does not fail.
- At runtime, both processes keep the last good Config when a reload fails, instead of erroring every search.

CONFIG EDITING (toml_edit): one ConfigDocument abstraction.
- Phase 1 contract, identical to Python where observable: an edited value keeps its key indentation, separator and trailing comment (the old value's decor is copied onto the new value). A missing key goes directly below the table header or the [[app]] id line; this is done by rebuilding the table's key order, because a key's leading comments travel with that key's decor. A missing table is appended as '[t]  # added by the settings window'.
- After every edit, the text is parsed back with the full loader and compared value by value, keeping Python's numeric leniency (1 == 1.0). The atomic write keeps the .agents.toml.tmp name with an fsync and copies the mode.
- Deliberate byte-level differences, all of which tomllib reads identically: strings are written as UTF-8 (fixes the emoji EditError); CRLF is preserved; numeric type follows the existing value (stops the 30 vs 30.0 flip); a symlinked agents.toml is written through to its target.
- Phase 3 adds structural ops: add/delete/rename/reorder [[app]], array edits that keep multi-line layout (via push_formatted and copied decor), nested command groups, [aliases] CRUD, [[routing.rule]] addressed by index with a signature check, and gateway including key_env. All ops are validated as a whole before the write.

LOGGING: a minimal stderr logger with the prefix 'llm-search: ' in both binaries. The lines 'running <argv0> in <cwd>' and 'opening <url before ?>' are kept, so the journalctl greps in the docs keep working.

PROCESSES: std::process::Command with stdio null, an unsafe pre_exec calling libc::setsid (equivalent to start_new_session), and a detached reaper thread calling wait(), so the resident box never accumulates zombies. Clipboard copy keeps using the wl-copy / xclip subprocess, for parity in the gio-only provider.

TESTS LAYOUT:
- crates/core/tests: one Rust test per Python unittest (same names) plus golden-vector tests reading tests/golden/*.json. tools/export_goldens.py runs against frozen v0.5.0 to produce those fixtures; it is deleted in Phase 2 and the fixtures stay.
- crates/cli/tests: gio::TestDBus integration tests, run one per test binary, that start the real built provider from a generated .service file.
- crates/ui/tests: #[gtk::test] under xvfb-run with GSK_RENDERER=cairo.

phases.name: Phase 3: Full settings editor (the next feature, Rust-only)
phases.goal: Make everything in agents.toml editable from the settings window, with whole-config validation before every save, while keeping the file's comments and layout.
deliverables:
Structural ops in core::edit, each a pure function DocumentMut → DocumentMut plus validation:
- [[app]]: add (appended after the last [[app]], prefixed with a blank line), duplicate, delete (the comments above its header go with it; trailing comment lines stay with the next header), move up and down (this changes tie order in ranking), rename id (offers to rewrite [aliases] values that point at the old id), and set any field.
- Field types: string (name, url, cwd, description, icon), bool (enabled, copy_prompt), number (priority), string arrays (requires, tags, models, efforts), and command argv with one level of nested optional groups.
- Arrays that are multi-line in the file keep that layout, using copied element decor, push_formatted and a trailing newline and comma. Single-line arrays stay single-line.
- [aliases]: add, delete, rename key, and set target, where the target is app, app:model or a gateway model.
- [routing]: low_effort_max_words, high_effort_patterns list, and [[routing.rule]] add, delete, reorder and set tag, patterns or weight. Rules are addressed by index plus a content fingerprint; an op fails if the file changed underneath.
- [gateway]: url, chat_url, auto_model, key_env. Renaming key_env offers to move the secret in secrets.env.
- Deleting a key returns it to the default.

Whole-config validation (core::validate), run on the edited in-memory document before any write. Checks: TOML syntax, the schema and types, duplicate app ids, empty or missing required fields, regex compile through pyre with the error position, alias targets that resolve, URL and chat_url template syntax ({effort} in chat_url is flagged), command placeholders, efforts outside EFFORTS (a warning, since gateway variants pass through), requires that are not found (a warning), and an existing cwd (a warning). Errors block the save and show inline on the field. Warnings show as row subtitles.

UI:
- The Agents page becomes a list of agent rows (enable switch, reorder, add and delete with AlertDialog confirmation) opening an adw::NavigationView subpage per agent with every field. The subpage stays reachable for disabled agents, which fixes SW-17.
- Command editor: argument rows and 'optional group' expanders, placeholder insert buttons, and a live argv preview rendered by core fill_command for a sample prompt.
- New Aliases page; on the Routing page, a rules list with a pattern editor and a 'test a prompt' field showing the matched tags and suggested effort through the real ranker.
- Gateway page gains key_env.
- An AdwBanner appears when agents.toml or secrets.env changes on disk while a subpage holds unapplied edits, with Reload / Keep mine (keep mine re-validates against the new file).

Save model: scalars keep today's instant-apply (spin and switch rows save on change, entry rows on apply). Compound edits (new agent, command, patterns list, rule) save on an explicit Apply in the subpage. Every save goes through validate → atomic write → reload.
Docs: CONFIGURATION.md and USAGE.md updated with screenshots of every page. The 'Add an Agent → Open agents.toml' row becomes an add button, and the file-open row stays.

phases.name: Phase 4: Deliberate behavior fixes, hardening and 1.0
phases.goal: Now that no second implementation constrains behavior, fix the known Python-era bugs one at a time, each a visible and reversible change, then call it 1.0.
deliverables:
Each fix is a separate commit that changes its golden case, with a CHANGELOG line. The candidate list needs owner approval item by item:
- An alias target written 'app:<id>' resolves.
- Alias targets split at the last ':' only when the prefix is a known app, so gateway models with ':' work.
- requires-path substitution applies only to literal template items, not to substituted prompt or model values.
- An @-requested row survives max_rows == 1, and max_rows <= 0 means no rows or is clamped by validation.
- chat_url gets {effort}.
- Folder-picker home prefix uses path components; get_path() None is handled.

plans.install_and_distribution:
MINIMUM PLATFORM, from the build features v4_14 / v1_5: GNOME 46 or newer stack. Runtime needs GTK ≥ 4.14, libadwaita ≥ 1.5, GLib ≥ 2.80, libsoup 3, glibc ≥ 2.39 for the prebuilt binaries, and a systemd user session (environment.d). Building from source needs Rust ≥ 1.92 (the MSRV of gtk-rs 0.22/0.11), a C toolchain and pkg-config.

FROM SOURCE (git clone, then `./install.sh [--shortcut '<Primary><Super>space'] [--name NAME]`; the bootstrap checks dependencies, builds with --locked and runs the Rust installer):
- Fedora 43 / 44 / 45 (tested on 44): `sudo dnf install rust cargo gcc pkgconf-pkg-config gtk4-devel libadwaita-devel glib2-devel libsoup3-devel wl-clipboard`. Distro rustc 1.99 works.
- Debian 13 (trixie): the stable rustc is 1.85.1, which is too old. Either `sudo apt install -t trixie-backports rustc cargo` (1.96.1) or use rustup. Then `sudo apt install build-essential pkg-config libgtk-4-dev libadwaita-1-dev libglib2.0-dev libsoup-3.0-dev wl-clipboard`. Debian 12 is unsupported (libadwaita 1.2).
- Ubuntu 26.04: `sudo apt install rustc cargo build-essential pkg-config libgtk-4-dev libadwaita-1-dev libglib2.0-dev libsoup-3.0-dev wl-clipboard`. Distro rustc 1.93.1 works.
- Ubuntu 24.04: the newest distro toolchain is rustc-1.91, which is too old, so use rustup (`curl … rustup.rs`, then `rustup default stable`) or the prebuilt tarball. Library packages are as for 26.04 (GTK 4.14.5, libadwaita 1.5.0 meet the baseline exactly).
- Arch / Manjaro / EndeavourOS: `sudo pacman -S --needed base-devel pkgconf rust gtk4 libadwaita libsoup3 wl-clipboard`.
- openSUSE Tumbleweed: `sudo zypper in rust cargo gcc pkgconf-pkg-config gtk4-devel libadwaita-devel glib2-devel libsoup-devel wl-clipboard`. The libsoup-devel name must be verified during Phase 2 smoke testing.
- Silverblue / Kinoite: build inside a toolbox with the Fedora package list. The installed binaries run on the host, which has the GTK and libadwaita runtime.

PREBUILT BINARIES (GitHub Releases, Phase 2 onward):
- Built on a pinned ubuntu-24.04 runner (never ubuntu-latest, which moves to 26.04 between 2026-10-19 and 2026-11-19 and would silently raise the glibc, GTK and libadwaita floor) with rustup stable and features v4_14 / v1_5, dynamically linked, stripped.
- Tarball agent-search-<ver>-x86_64-linux-gnu.tar.gz (optionally aarch64) plus SHA256SUMS and a provenance attestation.
- Runtime packages only:
  - Fedora: gtk4 libadwaita libsoup3
  - Debian/Ubuntu: libgtk-4-1 libadwaita-1-0 libsoup-3.0-0
  - Arch: gtk4 libadwaita libsoup3
  - Tumbleweed: libgtk-4-1 libadwaita-1-0 libsoup-3_0-0 (names to verify)
  - wl-clipboard is optional everywhere.
- Flow: download, run `sha256sum -c SHA256SUMS`, extract, then `./install.sh`. The bootstrap sees bin/llm-search and skips cargo.
- A container smoke matrix for every release covers Fedora 43/44, Debian 13, Ubuntu 24.04/26.04, Arch and Tumbleweed.

INSTALL FLOW (Rust installer, same steps and messages as today):
1. Check the runtime libraries; missing ones print the per-distro hint.
2. Seed ~/.llm-search/config without overwriting, and chmod 600 secrets.env.
3. Clean up legacy ids.
4. Render the .service, .desktop and ini files into ~/.llm-search/state/install. The Exec lines become `/usr/bin/env LLM_SEARCH_HOME=<home> <data>/llm-search/bin/llm-search search-provider` and `… <data>/llm-search/bin/agent-search --gapplication-service`.
5. Copy the binaries atomically into $XDG_DATA_HOME/llm-search/bin, so running processes keep the old inode.
6. Symlink the same six targets as today, including ~/.local/bin/llm-search pointing at the installed binary.
7. Write or keep environment.d and run the generator check.
8. Set the optional shortcut through gio::Settings.
9. Stop the old Python processes and the running Rust ones, then refresh the desktop database.
10. Print the same 'Done. Next steps' text.

Re-running install upgrades in place. A logout is needed only on a first install, as today. `uninstall [--purge]` reverses it, and now also removes the copied binaries.

DOCS: the README requirements table gets 'from source' and 'prebuilt' columns per distro. The Phase 0 interim fix for Python 0.5.0 corrects the minimums (GNOME 46+, not Fedora 39 or Debian 12) and the Debian/Ubuntu packages `python3-gi gir1.2-glib-2.0 gir1.2-gtk-4.0 gir1.2-adw-1`.

contracts_changed: Rendered .service Exec lines point at the installed Rust binaries (`llm-search search-provider` and `agent-search --gapplication-service`) instead of python3 -m. PYTHONPATH is no longer set, so launched agents stop inheriting it. Migration: re-running ./install.sh re-renders them; Phase 1 swaps only the prompt box, and Phase 2 swaps the provider.

~/.local/bin/llm-search becomes a symlink to $XDG_DATA_HOME/llm-search/bin/llm-search, a copied binary, instead of the repo's bash script. --copy becomes an accepted no-op. uninstall also removes the copied binaries.

Requirements change from Python 3.11 + PyGObject to the GTK ≥ 4.14, libadwaita ≥ 1.5 and libsoup3 runtime, plus Rust ≥ 1.92 to build. Prebuilt tarballs cover distros whose rustc is too old. install.sh becomes a small bash bootstrap that builds or detects the binaries, then runs the Rust installer.

`llm-search test` now runs `llm-search check` (config validation) rather than the Python unittest suite. The project's own tests are `cargo test`. New commands: `check` and `restart`. `status` gains extra lines. Dry-run says 'would remove' instead of 'removed'.

Process names change to llm-search (search-provider) and agent-search. The TROUBLESHOOTING pkill recipes are replaced by `llm-search restart`. The installer stops both the legacy Python processes and the Rust ones.

Routing patterns run on fancy-regex through a Python-compatibility translator. Known differences remain for Unicode \w/\b on combining marks, \s on U+001C..U+001F, and İ/ı case folding. \N{NAME}, (?a) and octal escapes are rejected. Invalid patterns are disabled with a diagnostic at load time, instead of failing searches that reach them.

Load errors are softer. Unknown keys in [[app]] or [[routing.rule]], a string where a list is expected, a non-bool `enabled`, and a NaN priority become warnings with defined coercions instead of a fatal TypeError or odd substring and per-character behavior. A broken config at runtime keeps the last good config instead of returning D-Bus errors. The loader accepts TOML 1.1 syntax, but the editor never writes it.

TOML writer byte format: strings are written as UTF-8 instead of \uXXXX escapes (emoji values now save); CRLF files keep CRLF; the numeric type follows the existing value (no more 30 vs 30.0 flip). A symlinked agents.toml is written through to its target instead of being replaced by a file. Several missing keys added to a new table keep edit order. secrets.env writes become atomic.
Gateway: models can be fetched in the first 60 s after boot. The prompt box and the settings Test button never block; gateway rows arrive asynchronously. The 0.5 s timeout now bounds DNS too.
URL templates support only {name} and the {{ }} escapes. Other str.format features (format specs, conversions, attribute access) are activation errors, and `check` flags them at load time.
Prompt-box idle timer: it is armed after a windowless D-Bus start, and the open-settings race is fixed.
Settings window (Phase 3): full structural editing, validation before every save, an explicit Apply for compound edits, disabled agents can be edited, and a key_env field.

Behavior fixes in Phase 4, each approved separately: 'app:<id>' alias targets, ':' in gateway model aliases, requires substitution only on literal items, @-row kept at max_rows 1, {effort} in chat_url, the folder-picker home prefix, shortcut-dialog key rules and name preservation, and a config-error row in search.

risks_and_mitigations: A Python/Rust ranking mismatch during the hybrid Phase 1 would make the prompt box and GNOME search disagree. Mitigation: goldens exported from v0.5.0, diff_ranking.sh over a 500-prompt corpus plus the owner's patterns, a DIVERGENCES.toml allowlist, and a short hybrid window (Phase 2 follows right away).

The Rust editor could write a file the Python provider or v0.5.0 cannot load, which would break the hybrid or the rollback. Mitigation: CI parses every editor output with tomllib and llm_search.config.load through Phase 3. The editor never emits TOML 1.1 syntax, and no new schema keys are allowed before 1.0. The owner should not hand-write TOML 1.1 syntax while Phase 1 is installed; this is documented.

User regexes behave differently or stop compiling. Mitigation: the Phase 0 pyre audit of the owner's real config, the translator for Python-only syntax, compilation at load with clear diagnostics, a disabled pattern instead of a failed search, and a backtrack limit. Fallback: glib::Regex (PCRE2), which needs no new dependency, if parity matters more than ReDoS bounds.

toml_edit decor surprises: multi-line arrays collapsing, comments moving when [[app]] blocks are deleted, key placement. Mitigation: Phase 1 implements placement explicitly and checks it with goldens; Phase 3 round-trip goldens assert that only the intended lines change, with inverse-op tests; Array::fmt() is never called on existing arrays.

MSRV 1.92 excludes distro rustc on Debian 13 stable and Ubuntu 24.04. Mitigation: prebuilt tarballs, backports and rustup documented per distro, and an MSRV CI job. Pinning gtk-rs 0.10 is rejected because it would mean a second dependency line.

A binary linked against newer GTK or libadwaita symbols fails to start on older distros (BIND_NOW). Mitigation: fixed v4_14 / v1_5 features, release builds on a pinned ubuntu-24.04 runner (never ubuntu-latest), and the container smoke matrix. Any feature-flag bump needs an owner decision because it drops distros.

gtk4-rs 0.11.x patch releases have changed APIs (save/restore added in 0.11.2, reverted in 0.11.5), and 0.12/0.23 is coming. Mitigation: commit Cargo.lock, build with --locked, and budget one deliberate upgrade per GNOME cycle.

D-Bus activation pitfalls: registering the object too late, overriding local_command_line, or IS_SERVICE on the prompt box would break activation. Mitigation: register in dbus_register as the gtk-rs example does; TestDBus activation tests through real .service files; the provider harness is validated against Python first.

Panics in GTK callbacks or D-Bus handlers abort the process, where PyGObject only printed. Mitigation: clippy lints that deny unwrap/expect outside tests, Result-returning handlers, catch_unwind at the D-Bus boundary, and fuzzing in Phase 4.
Zombie children in the resident prompt box. Mitigation: a reaper thread per spawn and a 100-launch test.

Upgrade leftovers: an old Python process keeps owning a bus name (up to 30 min for the box). Mitigation: the installer and `restart` stop legacy processes found by /proc cmdline and the Rust ones through the 'quit' action or SIGTERM; covered by the upgrade test.

soup3 adds a build dependency (libsoup3-devel) and has whole-second timeouts. Mitigation: the 500 ms limit is enforced with a Cancellable; libsoup3 is present on every GNOME system at runtime. Fallback: ureq, if the owner confirms the gateway is plain-HTTP localhost.

Scope creep in the Phase 3 editor (the nested command group UI, conflicts with external edits). Mitigation: the editor works only on the frozen schema, one level of nesting (matching what fill_command supports), and a banner-based reload/keep-mine flow instead of merging.

plans.angle: SIMPLEST-ARCHITECTURE. The end state is one Rust package that builds one binary, `llm-search`. Its argv dispatch covers three things: the user CLI and installer, an internal `provider` mode (a gio::Application that serves SearchProvider2), and an internal `app` mode (the adw::Application prompt box plus the settings window). The pure logic sits in a GTK-free library target inside the same package. There is no workspace, no meson, no build.rs, no Blueprint or GResource, no async runtime, no clap and no zbus. Templates and the icon are embedded with include_str!/include_bytes!. Every external contract (bus names, object paths, the .ini file, the desktop id, the gsettings path, the ~/.llm-search layout, the agents.toml schema and its comments, the CLI verbs) stays as it is; anything that does change is listed below. The quickest route there has four phases after a short baseline. (0) Freeze Python, record parity vectors and fix the README. (1) Port the core library with tests. (2) Build the binary: provider, prompt box and Rust installer. The owner then cuts over and dogfoods it on his own machine, with the settings action temporarily opening agents.toml. (3) Build the new full settings editor directly on toml_edit; the old settings window is never ported, because it would be thrown away. (4) CI, prebuilt binaries, docs, then the 1.0 release. The only migration scaffolding is one script that dumps parity vectors from Python. Python and Rust never run side by side, and no compatibility shims are written.
plans.architecture:
END STATE (one package, one binary, two processes at runtime, the same two bus names as today) ```mermaid flowchart LR Shell[GNOME Shell] -- SearchProvider2 --> P["llm-search provider
(gio::Application, IS_SERVICE, 60 s idle)"] P -- "ActivateAction('search')" --> A["llm-search app --gapplication-service
(adw::Application: prompt box + settings)"] Key[gsettings shortcut / desktop Exec] --> C["llm-search prompt [TEXT]"] -- "Activate / ActivateAction + platform-data" --> A P & A & C --> L["lib: query, rank, catalog, launch, config, secrets, edit, pattern, gateway"] L --> F[("~/.llm-search/config/agents.toml + secrets.env")] ``` Why two processes and not one: merging the provider into the prompt box would change BusName in the .ini and drop a .service file. It would also keep a GTK process resident just for overview searches, and it would tangle two idle policies (60 s versus [prompt] idle_minutes). Two modes of one binary keep every D-Bus contract byte for byte. Provider mode never calls gtk::init, so it starts fast. PACKAGE LAYOUT (single Cargo package; edition 2024; rust-version = "1.92"; Cargo.lock committed; builds use --locked) - src/lib.rs (crate `agent_search`, GTK-free: no gtk/adw/gio/glib imports, enforced by a CI grep): - query.rs (parse, EFFORT_ALIASES, a py_split that adds \x1c-\x1f to char::is_whitespace) - rank.rs (rank, matched_tags, score, clamp_effort, suggest_effort, resolve, Row title/subtitle with ASCII-exact capitalize, result_id with blake2s-48, parse_result_id) - catalog.rs (app_candidates, models_from_info) - launch.rs (fill_url, fill_command, command_for, a `which` with an injectable PATH lookup used by the tests, and launch-plan building that returns a LaunchPlan {Copy, Spawn{argv,cwd}, OpenUri}) - config.rs (serde-typed Config, load(dir) -> Result, validate() that collects every semantic error with paths like app[2].command[3], signature(), home()/config_dir() with the exact LLM_SEARCH_HOME semantics) - secrets.rs (read_env_file parity, an atomic set_secret) - edit.rs (ConfigDoc over toml_edit::DocumentMut: typed operations, decor-preserving replace, atomic save, restore_defaults, legacy settings.toml migration) - pattern.rs (fancy-regex compile and match, plus a lint for constructs whose meaning differs from Python) - gateway.rs (blocking fetch with ureq, Option cache with 60 s TTL and 30 s back-off; every error yields []) - src/main.rs: argv dispatch. `provider` and `app` are internal; the rest is the CLI. - src/provider.rs: a small gio::Application subclass (ObjectSubclass boilerplate, about 50 lines) so that ApplicationImpl::dbus_register can register the object before the name is acquired. - src/prompt.rs: adw::Application with no subclass. State lives in Rc>, the UI is built in code as the Python version does, and the CSS is loaded with CssProvider::load_from_string. - src/settings/: window.rs, general.rs, agents.rs (list and per-agent subpage), routing.rs, aliases.rs, gateway.rs, and widgets.rs (a reusable StringListGroup and a debounced SpinRow). - src/shortcut.rs: gio::Settings with a SettingsSchemaSource lookup first. The CLI and the settings window share it. - src/cli/: install.rs, uninstall.rs, status.rs, query.rs, prompt.rs, check.rs. - share/*.in and the svg stay in the repo and are embedded at compile time. examples/config stays. HOW EACH PYTHON PIECE MAPS - Provider: gio::Application with IS_SERVICE and set_inactivity_timeout(60000). dbus_register chains up, then calls connection.register_object(path, &DBusNodeInfo::for_xml(INTERFACE_XML)?.lookup_interface(..)).method_call(closure).build(), reusing the Python XML. Inside the closure: `let _g = app.hold();`, parse params with Variant::get::<(Vec,)>(), and reply with invocation.return_value. Metas go out as Vec> (aa{sv}) with gicon = gio::ThemedIcon::new(icon).to_string(). Errors use return_dbus_error("org.freedesktop.DBus.Error.Failed", msg); no handler can panic, because all of them return Result. LaunchSearch is a fire-and-forget connection.call to ActivateAction('search', [], {}). Searches stay synchronous, as today. The gateway fetch is bounded by ureq's global 0.5 s timeout, which also covers DNS. - Prompt box: adw::Application with the default flags, run with run_with_args([argv0, rest...]) so that --gapplication-service keeps working. local_command_line is never overridden and IS_SERVICE is never hard-coded. Actions are 'search'(s) and 'preferences'. Startup takes one hold guard that stays alive for the life of the process. The window and its key handling follow PB-01..18. Gateway rows load through gio::spawn_blocking, awaited from glib::MainContext::spawn_local: app rows show at once and the cached or fetched model rows merge in afterwards. Launched children use std::process::Command with process_group(0) and Stdio::null(); a waiter thread reaps each one. URIs open through gtk::UriLauncher in the prompt box (it passes the activation token) and through gio::AppInfo::launch_default_for_uri in the provider, as Python does. - Settings: an adw::ApplicationWindow containing a ToolbarView, a HeaderBar with a ViewSwitcher, a ToastOverlay and a ViewStack. The Agents and Routing pages each sit in an adw::NavigationView so they can push subpages. Built only from v1_5-or-older widgets: EntryRow, PasswordEntryRow, SpinRow, SwitchRow, ExpanderRow, ComboRow, AlertDialog, Dialog, Banner. ButtonRow (1.6) is not used. - Config loading: toml 1.1.8 with serde derive. [[app]] and [[routing.rule]] use #[serde(deny_unknown_fields)], as today; other tables ignore unknown keys. A small `lenient_f64` deserializer accepts an int or a float for priority, weight and idle_minutes. After deserializing, validate() compiles every regex, checks that app ids are unique and match [A-Za-z0-9._-]+, checks url and command templates (only {prompt}/{model}/{effort} and {{ }} are allowed), and checks that alias targets name an existing app (an unknown gateway model is only a warning). - Editing: toml_edit 0.25.17. ConfigDoc has these operations: set_scalar, set_string_array (keeps the existing single-line or multi-line layout), set_command (items are a string or an array of strings), add_app, remove_app, rename_app (which offers to rewrite alias targets), set_alias/remove_alias, add_rule/remove_rule/move_rule, and remove_key. A replaced value keeps the old value's decor, so the key indentation, the '=' spacing and the trailing comment survive. A missing key is appended at the end of its table, which is toml_edit's default. A missing table is appended with the suffix ' # added by the settings window'. save() serializes, runs a full load()+validate() on the result, refuses to write on any error, and otherwise writes '.agents.toml.tmp' next to the canonicalized target (which keeps symlinks), with fsync, the mode copied from the old file, and a rename. If nothing changed, nothing is written. - Regex: fancy-regex 0.19.2 through RegexBuilder::new(p).case_insensitive(true).build(), compiled once at load. is_match stands in for re.search, and a BacktrackLimitExceeded result counts as no match and is logged. glib::Regex (PCRE2) was rejected because it would pull glib into the core and has no backtrack guard. The plain regex crate was rejected because it has no lookaround or backrefs. - IDs: blake2 0.10 (Blake2sVar::new(6)), so the 12-hex query key matches Python's exactly. - URL encoding: a hand-written quote (unreserved = ALPHA DIGIT _ . - ~, uppercase %XX), about 15 lines; no crate. - HTTP: ureq 3.4.2 with default-features=false (plain HTTP), plus serde_json; the JSON is walked as serde_json::Value so shape errors return [] instead of failing. HTTPS is an open question. - Logging: eprintln!("llm-search: {msg}"), the same journal prefix as today, with no logging crate. - CLI: hand-parsed argv, about 120 lines, with the same usage text, messages and exit codes 0/1/2. `prompt` makes the org.freedesktop.Application Activate or ActivateAction call itself through gio::bus_get_sync, with platform-data built from XDG_ACTIVATION_TOKEN and DESKTOP_STARTUP_ID, so the gapplication binary is no longer needed. `query` calls GetInitialResultSet and prints the reply with Variant::print(true), the same output as gdbus. DEPENDENCIES (complete list): gtk4 0.11.5 [v4_14], libadwaita 0.9.2 [v1_5] (glib and gio come through gtk::glib/gtk::gio), toml 1.1.8, toml_edit 0.25.17, serde 1 [derive], serde_json 1, fancy-regex 0.19.2, blake2 0.10, ureq 3.4.2 [no default features]. No dev-dependencies beyond std; tempdirs are created by hand under std::env::temp_dir. Release profile: lto="thin", codegen-units=1, strip=true. Expect roughly 4-6 MB stripped (an estimate). The Rust code should come to about 4,000-5,000 lines including the new editor, plus about 1,500 lines of tests.

phases.name: Phase 3: Full settings editor on toml_edit
phases.goal: Ship the next feature directly in Rust. A settings window can edit everything in agents.toml (search, prompt, agents with every field including add/delete/rename, aliases, routing patterns and rules, and the gateway including key_env and the secret), with the whole config validated before each save and comments preserved.
deliverables: edit.rs complete: add_app (pushed after the last [[app]], with a blank-line prefix), remove_app (the comments above that entry's header go with it), rename_app (rewrites matching [aliases] targets if the user confirms), set_string_array (keeps a multi-line array multi-line: prefix '\n    ', trailing '\n', trailing comma), set_command (one array item per row; a single part is written as a string and several parts as an array, which is lossless because fill_command wraps strings), aliases CRUD (lowercase keys), rules add/remove/move up/down, remove_key (restores a default by deleting the key), and set_key_env.

Settings window: a ViewSwitcher with General, Agents, Aliases, Routing and Gateway pages. General keeps today's rows (the shortcut, Keep Running, Results, Configuration Files, Restore Defaults with an AlertDialog). Agents: a list with a SwitchRow per agent, 'Add Agent' (an adw::Dialog asking for id, name and kind (URL or Command) with live validation), and a NavigationView subpage per agent. The subpage holds name, id (rename), enabled, kind, url, a command editor with one EntryRow per item (parsed and displayed through glib::shell_parse_argv/shell_quote), a live 'Runs: …' preview with sample values, cwd with a folder picker that fixes the home-prefix bug, requires, icon, tags, models, efforts (five check rows), priority, copy_prompt, description, and 'Delete Agent…' (an AlertDialog). Aliases: rows of name -> target, with a target suggestion list built from the apps and their models. Routing: low_effort_max_words, a high_effort_patterns list, and a rule subpage (tag, weight, patterns) with add, delete and move. Every pattern row shows its compile error or lint warning inline. Gateway: url, chat_url, auto_model, key_env, the key, and an asynchronous Test button.
widgets.rs: one reusable StringListGroup used for every string array, and a SpinRow that saves 600 ms after the last change.

Save model: GNOME-style instant apply. Each committed change (entry apply, switch, debounced spin, dialog confirm) becomes one ConfigDoc operation, then a full validation, then an atomic save, then app.reload(). On a validation error the file is left alone, a toast reads "Couldn't save: <path>: <message>", and the widget goes back to the value in the document. An agents.toml that is already invalid on disk shows an adw::StatusPage with the error and an 'Open agents.toml' button, and editing is disabled.

External edits: a 300 ms debounced file monitor plus a signature check. It rebuilds the pages, returns to the same agent or rule subpage by id or index when it still exists, and shows the toast 'Updated from agents.toml'. The pending timer is removed when the window closes.

examples/config/agents.toml: the comments now point to `llm-search check` instead of python3 tomllib, the regex note says the patterns use fancy-regex syntax, and the 'Add an Agent' wording no longer says agents can only be added in the file.
phases.user_visible_state: Owner build: the full settings editor replaces the temporary 'Open agents.toml'. Everything in agents.toml can be edited from the UI, and comments and formatting survive edits.

CRLF fixtures are checked against whatever toml_edit preserves, and the result is documented. Operation golden tests: each operation's output must equal a committed expected file, and the diff must be limited to the target entry. Validation tests: every invalid input (duplicate id, bad regex, unknown placeholder, wrong type, empty id, an id containing '|' or ':') is refused and the file is left untouched. #[gtk::test] scenarios under xvfb drive the widgets directly, not by synthesizing input: add an agent and assert the file contains it, rename it and assert the alias was rewritten, delete it, add a rule pattern, enter an invalid pattern and assert the file is unchanged and the row shows an error. plans.install_and_distribution:
TWO INSTALL PATHS, ONE INSTALLER (`llm-search install`, run through ./install.sh)

1. Prebuilt (recommended; no toolchain needed). Download llm-search-<ver>-x86_64-linux.tar.gz from GitHub Releases, check it against SHA256SUMS, unpack it and run `./install.sh [--name NAME] [--shortcut '<Primary><Super>space']`. The binary is built on a pinned ubuntu-24.04 runner with gtk4 feature v4_14 and libadwaita feature v1_5, and links dynamically against the system GTK and libadwaita. Runtime minimums: glibc 2.39, GTK 4.14, libadwaita 1.5, plus GNOME Shell for search. Optional: wl-clipboard (or xclip) for copy_prompt, and xdg-utils.
   Runtime packages (GNOME desktops usually have them already):
   - Fedora: gtk4 libadwaita
   - Debian/Ubuntu: libgtk-4-1 libadwaita-1-0
   - Arch: gtk4 libadwaita
   - openSUSE: libgtk-4-1 libadwaita-1-0
   Supported: Fedora 42+ (tested on 44), Debian 13, Ubuntu 24.04 and 26.04, Arch, openSUSE Tumbleweed. Not supported: Debian 12 (libadwaita 1.2) and Fedora 39 (GTK/libadwaita too old).

2. From source (git clone, then ./install.sh, which runs `cargo build --release --locked` and then installs). The build needs Rust 1.92 or newer, a C linker, pkg-config, and the GTK4 and libadwaita development files.
   - Fedora 43/44/45: `sudo dnf install rust cargo gcc pkgconf-pkg-config gtk4-devel libadwaita-devel` (distro rustc 1.99 works).
   - Debian 13: `sudo apt install -t trixie-backports rustc cargo`, then `sudo apt install build-essential pkg-config libgtk-4-dev libadwaita-1-dev`. Stable trixie rustc 1.85 is too old; rustup also works.
   - Ubuntu 24.04: distro rustc tops out at 1.91, so install Rust with rustup (https://rustup.rs), then `sudo apt install build-essential pkg-config libgtk-4-dev libadwaita-1-dev`.
   - Ubuntu 26.04: `sudo apt install rustc cargo build-essential pkg-config libgtk-4-dev libadwaita-1-dev` (rustc 1.93).
   - Arch: `sudo pacman -S --needed base-devel rust gtk4 libadwaita`.
   - openSUSE Tumbleweed: `sudo zypper in rust cargo gcc pkgconf-pkg-config gtk4-devel libadwaita-devel`.
   For running the tests, also: dbus-daemon and Xvfb (Fedora: dbus-daemon xorg-x11-server-Xvfb; Debian/Ubuntu: dbus-daemon xvfb; Arch: xorg-server-xvfb).

WHAT install DOES (same steps and messages as the bash version; the differences are marked):
- Checks that no path contains a space.
- Seeds config/agents.toml and secrets.env without overwriting existing files, and runs chmod 600 on secrets.env.
- Migrates a legacy settings.toml.
- Removes the old io.github.oscillatingjem.LlmSearchProvider links.
- NEW: copies the binary atomically to ~/.local/share/llm-search/bin/llm-search.
- Renders the three templates into ~/.llm-search/state/install and copies the .ini and svg there.
- Symlinks the same six targets as before; ~/.local/bin/llm-search links to the installed binary.
- Writes ~/.config/environment.d/60-llm-search.conf with the identical line and runs the generator safety check.
- Sets the shortcut when --shortcut is given.
- Stops both the Python and the Rust processes.
- Runs update-desktop-database.
- Runs `check` and prints its warnings.
- Prints the 'Done. Next steps:' text.
`--copy` is accepted and has no effect (the binary is always copied); it prints a note. `--dry-run` works as before. Upgrading from 0.5 is one run of ./install.sh followed by logging out and back in.

NOT IN SCOPE FOR 1.0: Flatpak (the sandbox gets in the way of exporting a search provider and of spawning host agent commands without flatpak-spawn --host), distro packages (COPR or AUR could come later; open question), and `cargo install` (it would not install the desktop, D-Bus or .ini files, although `llm-search install` run after it would).

The marker '[<table>]  # added by the settings window' is still used.
